sections.overview: The firemouth cichlid is a freshwater fish native to the Yucatán region and nearby Central America.
sections.identification: It reaches about 17 cm in total length and is named for the bright reddish area beneath its head.
sections.habitat: It inhabits rivers, canals and ponds, including slow-flowing water with muddy or sandy bottoms and shoreline vegetation.
sections.diet: Its diet varies; a study in a Yucatán lagoon found substantial zooplankton feeding, while broader accounts also report algae and other food.
sections.behavior: It is associated with shallow, vegetated freshwater habitats; feeding can vary with season, time and fish size.
sections.reproduction: Pairs lay eggs on open surfaces and both parents guard them; they later move the young into shallow pits and continue guarding them.
sections.ecology: It is a benthopelagic omnivore whose recorded food includes zooplankton and algae; diet studies show variation among habitats and seasons.
sections.conservation: A 2018 global assessment listed it as Least Concern.
